en: [Rumbling as though speaking,]
Springs overflowed, cliffs collapsed,
Such was the terror he displayed.
When the great sage heard this,
Unable to find a remedy,
His wits fled and strength failed,
Exhausted, he cried in distress,
God forbid such a sight,
If a scout leaves us in this state,
[When his mighty lion comes,]
What shall we do then?
[If his foremost man leaves us thus,]
If his khan, the warrior Seytek, comes,
If the earth breaks and sways,
What shall we do then?
[Joltoy is a tiger-like servant,]
[For the city whose road is harsh,]
This is the calamity we have met,
[Both hardship and a mountain pass,]
[A tale of much consequence for the people,]
That ill-fated Akjoltoy,
Is one of the renowned warriors,
Meeting upon the battlefield,
Fighting hard and long,
Pitting sorcerous tricks against each other,
Grappling without sparing life,
[The fire-burning killer,]
[Without waiting, testing his condition,]
[He killed those who commanded,]
Let me face this enemy as an enemy,
How great is his strength and reach?
[Of that clamorous wretch,]
Let me measure him and learn his secret.
[If he is merely a lone, lean warrior,]
[If his valor falls even a tooth short,]
I shall cut off his head,
Split his belly like a melon,
Cut off his head like a sheep's.
I shall return and tell of his strength.
[Of that clamorous battle cry,]
I shall get to its very root.
When he saw Akjoltoy's uproar,
Pouring out wrath, bellowing,
As if misfortune had struck his wife,
Calling his champions,
Camp by day and drive them at night,
Scout the land without missing a day,
[Set guards surveying the surrounding land,]
Before the renowned khan Kiche,
[When the time comes, of the Manchu,]
Let no shadow crush our hopes,
Let every heart be opened,
[For lordship and for the lord,]
[There is no wisdom in that great swine,]
Do not disturb the horses' order,
Keep driving my horses,
For six days, then seven,
[Keep the army encamped between.]
[Make them known to the rulers,]
Never sated when tasting blood,
[Saying this to his attendant,]
He said this to his watchman,
When the great gun cracked,
He was a warrior who did not flinch,
When the black gun boomed,
[They opened their palms and acclaimed him,]
[The tumult that would follow him,]
They discerned it all without omission,
Confirming others' words,
Great was the nation of Kakan,
[They heard him as their great lord.]
[Speaking words that would endure in the world,]
[The false world allotted to one's head,]
Rebuking the foolish,
Before he closed his mouth after speaking,
[A roar came along the ridge,]
The one who dwelt in Ala-Too,
[Who never yielded his privilege to anyone,]
If there was an enemy or foe,
[He never showed the least fear,]
[His people never sated with blood,]
[Seeing a break, he roared,]
God forbid you face him,
His purpose became clear.
[From Joltoy's heroism,]
Seeing the true measure of his worth,
God forbid you face him,
What will become of me? he thought.
[His bearing weighty and imposing,]
[His valor and appearance,]
He would slaughter whoever challenged him,
He would slaughter many lives,
In life, his sight was clear,
[Renowned among men, supremely wise,]
An exceptional judge, keen-eyed,
Standing tall, scattering his wrath,
It was the moment his wrath rose.
Thus the great wise one spoke,
Telling this [to the khan beside him],
Until his precious head entered the earth,
He said, do not surrender your honor.
Without honor there is no conscience.
To subdue the Kyrgyz [host],
You came from the khagan [arising],
[Taunting, with swords passing],
[His executioners passing high],
To die if his appointed death came,
For honor and for his people,
[Raging and roaring],
[Like an exceptionally mighty infidel],
Without rushing or paying heed,
This Beijing man was no wise one.
He did not reckon him worth a hem.
Ak Joltoy, without leaping about,
Who had seen a fight like this?
Kulan Sur, the mountainlike steed,
Joltoy, who came from his company,
Upon seeing this man,
[That side rose in dust],
Kulan Sur, the mountainlike steed,
Now drew back and turned his head.
He rejoiced at the word enemy,
Clad entirely in iron,
Taking a [steel-shafted] spear,
Girding on a bare sword,
A great man who came from Beijing,
He was an enormous warrior.
[Ninety beasts slaughtered for his feast],
[Mounted on a six-month-old remount],
He settled disputes that troubled heads,
He conquered enemies on the march.
He demonstrated a lion's courage.
In Beijing, the people of forty khans,
He brought under one [enclosure].
[His terror was vast, his fury great],
When he roared, [from the darkness],
One cried, I am dead, abandoning hope of life.
[With bristling whiskers],
Once, many people together,
His opponent was Ak Joltoy.
He began a fierce quarrel.
Raging and thundering,
He left utterly exhausted.
Roaring with fearsome menace,
[The lion of a divided mountain],
[Striking the great trumpet with a whip],
In your stammering tongue,
You are my enemy in your heart.
If I flick you lightly, your strength leaves.
[If strength remains after a measured blow],
[I shall break your might into a thousand pieces].
I shall scatter your honor like ashes.
And if my spirit [stiffens],
If that thing remained as broad as the earth,
From today onward, ride forth,
Saying, “I turned back and broke through,”
From the lone dark Kyrgyz,
Saying, “I handed his bow into their hands,”
I shall tell Jadyger,
Saying, “I turned and made them Kyrgyz,”
I shall draw toward the Kalmyks,
If no evil remains among my people,
I shall find it among my people,
The evil Kalmyks of my people,
Turning away on a day of repudiation,
The Kalmyk enemy of old,
Leave one behind and let a thousand come,
Leave your thousand and come yourself,
The turmoil of the age,
Let all the guns of the age come,
If I join them, there are fifty arrows,
A mounted man makes a great battle,
You came from afar and saw it,
Can a man exist without ever lying down?
You shall see his great bow,
Now you alone, Joltoy,
You shall turn and seize them together,
The elder who pastured the livestock,
He went about spreading his lineage,
If you do not turn from your corruption,
You will die without understanding,
These men overwhelmed your thousand.
When it remains, send it back,
Cover your head against the harsh wind,
The Kyrgyz are now your death,
Sitting beneath the banner, he was cut down,
The Kyrgyz who stood in the right,
I bound my strength upon my back,
His stirring turmoil,
My misfortune boiled over,
May he not enter the snare through oppression,
Protect those in the army,
You made the poor man prosper,
Let me spend the night circling,
Without striking you, the vagrant passed,
May he not throw your people into uproar,
If I do not bring it to a complete end,
To the enemy whose tongue roamed,
If you rise, poor Kyrgyz,
If I do not gather the rounded stones,
If I do not strike a thousand upon the forehead,
If I do not find him within one month,
If I do not strike in the returning month,
May I die without knowing,
Would it be right for me to endure this?
A man drew near and recited the bow-prayer,
Now he was a warrior known through his father,
Now you were the head of the blue-blooded khan,
Now these were his own sorrowful words.
Thus spoke Chong Bilgich,
He poured out all of his wrath,
He did not tire of resisting,
His stately bearing collapsed,
The people within the fortress fled,
Such was the appearance of their fear,
Lifting up his komuz,
He rumbled in anger,
Send the gracious bride back,
The beauty bestowed by Ala-Too,
If I contend with his fierce bearing,
Many thousands of Kyrgyz gathered to meet,
I am Chong Bilgich,
It was an event unlike any other,
The whole world had assembled,
They learned from his fearsome presence,
Countless children were afraid,
Of their number, I alone remained,
I knew the strength of the wandering warrior,
Weighing themselves against the stag,
He fell, saying it was his due,
Saying, “What I gave to Joltoy,”
Of the unwary sage from Beijing,
Saying that the color had left your face,
He went asking it of the idol,
My pure wish has now come,
This Joltoy is the one I desired,
The time came to have him struck down,
Would the man who seized him draw back?
Would the thoughtful warrior return?
Thus spoke Chong Bilgich,
Rejoicing, he staked out the sands,
He was revealed when the khan’s arrow struck,
Livestock remained when he longed for the girl,
The enemy rose from his place and remained,
Frightened by a demon, he recoiled,
Saying his gray turban was ready,
The hero’s wish,
Saying, “I shall spill Ak Joltoy’s blood,”
To cast the Kyrgyz down in disgrace,
They gathered like ringing bells,
To drive them toward that place,
Mighty Joltoy had indeed exerted his strength,
Chong Bilgich had rejoiced,
The great hound fixed its eyes upon the ground,
Upon that very hound,
The gray beast had no tooth that could break it,
